correctness.rationale: Nonempty selected original edges meet at least two parts, so every unused original vertex has a permanently observed edge into the selected endpoint set. The initially unseen line-graph vertices are precisely edges among unused vertices. A cycle cannot be forced, because the first observed edge of that cycle would require forcing from a vertex adjacent to two unobserved cycle edges. Conversely leaf elimination in an unused-edge forest works using the observed boundary edge at the leaf. The complete-multipartite forest classification is exactly one nonempty part or two with a part of size one. Inclusion–exclusion on used vertices yields the polynomial. Minimum-size rook and triangular sets are exhaustively classified by row-support and matchings/one wedge, respectively. An independent direct forcing simulation agreed for 27 graph profiles and 255318 subsets.

value.rationale: Theorem translates a dynamic graph-observation process into an exact induced-forest obstruction for every line graph of a complete multipartite graph, providing the complete cardinality distribution rather than only the minimum. The same structure yields closed counts of minimum PMU placements for every rook graph and every triangular graph, independently motivated by sensor-placement multiplicities and graph polynomial enumeration. The formula is a genuine structural refinement of the known scalar rook value; arbitrary part profiles and all sizes are treated.
